name: Mark

facts.author: John Mark, a companion of Peter and of Paul. The early church held that Mark wrote down what Peter preached about Jesus.
facts.audience: Christians outside Judea, very likely in Rome, many of them not Jews

about: Mark is the shortest of the four Gospels and moves quickly. It tells little of Jesus' words compared with His deeds: He heals the sick, drives out demons, calms the storm and feeds the crowds, and the word "immediately" appears again and again.

The first half asks who Jesus is, and the answer comes when Peter says that He is the Christ (8:29). From then on Jesus turns toward Jerusalem and teaches His disciples that the Son of man must suffer, die and rise again. More than a third of the book covers the last week of His life, His death on the cross and the empty tomb.

themes.title: Jesus the Son of God
themes.text: The book opens by calling Jesus the Son of God, and at the cross a Roman centurion says the same.

themes.title: The servant who gives His life
themes.text: Jesus came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.

themes.title: Following Jesus
themes.text: The disciples often fail to understand, yet Jesus calls them to take up their cross and follow Him.

themes.title: Good news for all nations
themes.text: Mark explains Jewish customs for readers who did not know them, and the gospel is to be preached to every nation.
